item.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob

item.title: Interpolation in the Inquisitive Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.32366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that each of the infinitely many extensions of the basic inquisitive logic has the Craig interpolation property, and deduce from this that each of these extensions also has the Beth definability property. These results stand in contrast to existing characterizations of interpolation within lattices of extensions, in which the distribution of logics with interpolation is sparse.
item.dc:creator: Josef v. H. Doyle, Wesley Fussner

item.title: On the complexity of Medvedev reducibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.32522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Medvedev lattice is a tool used to classify the complexity of effective closed sets. In this article, we are interested in the complexity of using this tool. In particular, we study the complexity of deciding whether two effective closed sets have the same degree, when one is fixed and the other is given as input. This problem is naturally~$\Sigma^0_3$, and among other results, we show that for all degrees except the maximal one, the problem reaches its maximal complexity. It turns out that the argument is not uniform and depends on the self-similarity of the fixed degree, a notion that we introduce in this article. The complexity of having maximal degree is particularly difficult to establish, but we obtain a lower bound that almost matches the upper bound. We also show that deciding whether an effective closed set has a degree incomparable with a fixed degree $d$ is $\Pi^0_3$-complete whenever $\mathbf{0}_s <_s d <_s \mathbf{1}_s$.
item.dc:creator: Remi Pallen

item.title: Adversarial Problems and the Limits of Uniform Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2512.08149v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A general method of resolution can take part in forming problems once their language represents the method itself. A fixed formation rule gives each sound resolver a presentation it cannot answer. Admitting the diagnosis yields a sound successor with an instance of its own. For standard arithmetical theories $\mathrm{T}$, the instance is $\mathsf{HA}$-provably equivalent to $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{T})$. A theory that decides its own instance asserts a false sentence. The $m$-th iterated independence question is equivalent to the instance $m$ stages later. No effective admission policy with consistent union closes the regress. A noncomputable answer function resolves all program indices, while a false assertion of resolution supplies no warrant. At feasible scale, bounded self-consistency is cheap. A clocked G\"odel sentence gives an unconditional gap relative to its short binary description, but no superpolynomial lower bound in the window size. The arithmetic identity motivates studying bounded consistency of the successor theory, as in a conjecture of Pudl\'ak. We state its finitely axiomatized case and prove that it implies $\mathcal{NP}\ne\mathrm{co}\mathcal{NP}$. The conjecture motivates a feasible analogue, but does not establish all clauses of the unbounded barrier.
item.dc:creator: Milan Rosko

item.title: The computable functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2606.05456v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the continuous functional calculus is computable. As consequences we obtain the computable compactness of the spectrum of any computable normal element of a computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra, the existence of effective approximate units for computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras, and an effective version of the Spectral Theorem for compact operators on separable Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. Eagle, Timothy H. McNicholl

item.title: The universal measure of nonstochastic objects
item.description: arXiv:2608.27098v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The usual settings for discussing the notion of stochastic objects are very different from Kolmogorov's original structure-free setting, in which there is no predefined external structure on the objects (such as the lengths of binary strings). A natural modification of stochasticity, obtained by replacing finite sets as models with probability measures, is quasi-stochasticity. The structure-free setting is common in studies of quasi-stochasticity, and known results show that the universal machine generates non-quasi-stochastic objects with exponentially small probability. This paper shows that, on the other hand, the universal machine generates nonstochastic objects surprisingly often. It also systematically explores numerous connections between stochasticity and quasi-stochasticity in the structure-free setting. In particular, the definition of quasi-stochasticity can be modified in a natural way modelled on Kolmogorov's definition so that non-quasi-stochastic objects are produced as often as nonstochastic ones; the results for this modification imply all the results of this paper showing that nonstochastic objects are frequent.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Vovk

item.title: Comparing the automorphism group of the measure algebra with some groups related to the infinite permutation group of the natural numbers
item.description: arXiv:math/0312472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove, by a straight construction, that the automorphism group of the measure algebra and the subgroup of the measure preserving ones cannot be isomorphic to the trivial automorphisms of P(N)/fin.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Ursino

item.title: Generalized fluctuation bounds for stochastic algorithms in the presence of compactness
item.description: arXiv:2602.22741v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a convergence result for sequences of random variables taking values in a metric space that satisfy a stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotonicity condition, in the context of a (local) compactness assumption. Our result is quantitative in that we derive an explicit and effective construction which, in terms of only a few moduli representing quantitative witnesses to key properties of the sequence of random variables and the underlying metric space involved, provides a metastable rate of pointwise convergence, a type of generalized fluctuation bound. That quantitative result in particular relies on the development of a finitary theory of martingales, culminating in a fully finitary Robbins-Siegmund theorem. We outline how this result particularises to the circumstances of the seminal work of Combettes and Pesquet on stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotone sequences in separable Hilbert spaces, and we provide an initial application by illustrating how these results can be used to provide a metastable rate of pointwise convergence for a stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann scheme solving a stochastic common fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps over proper Hadamard spaces. This work is set in the context of recent applications of the logic-based methodology of proof mining to probability theory, and represents its most sophisticated case study to date.
item.dc:creator: Morenikeji Neri, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell

item.title: Commutative coherent rings with $\mathcal{GP}\not\subseteq\mathcal{GF}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.17748v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every field $k$, we construct a commutative coherent $k$-algebra admitting a Gorenstein projective module that is not Gorenstein flat.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang
